newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia cracks down on opposition alliance.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia cracks down on opposition alliance.

text.p: Indonesia has cracked down on a growing alliance between supporters of a Moslem-based minority party and the ousted leader of a rival party ahead of the May 29 general election, military and state officials said on Tuesday.

Lieutenant-General Syarwan Hamid, the armed forces chief of socio-political affairs, said authorities banned the display of banners and pictures of Megawati Sukarnoputri of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) at campaign rallies organised by the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP).
"There will be action (against the display of Megawati's pictures and banners)," he told reporters at the sidelines of a rally organised by the government-backed PDI.
"We will be persuasive...we will ask campaign participants not to show them. We want everybody to obey the rules. We want the campaign to proceed smoothly," he said without elaborating.
Supporters of Megawati, daughter of late founding president Sukarno, have been attending rallies of the PPP carrying her pictures and banners depicting an alliance between the two.
The star, which is the PPP's symbol, and banners and flags emblazoned "Mega-Bintang" have been waved at many PPP rallies.

Megawati was removed as PDI chief by a government-backed faction last year and has been barred from the elections. She had asked her supporters not to take part in the campaign, but appears to have tacitly approved the link-up with the PPP.
The PPP and the PDI are battling the ruling Golkar party for 425 elected seats in the 500-member parliament. The rest of the seats are allocated for the military, whose members do not vote.

The official Antara news agency quoted Interior Minister Yogie Memet as saying on Monday that the display of banners and pictures suggesting alliance between Megawati and PPP had been banned. It gave no details.

Meanwhile, Attorney-General Singgih on Tuesday urged the three poll contestants to uphold the law in order to avoid violence in the wake of recent clashes among party supporters during the election campaign, which started last month.
"We should uphold the law," Singgih, chairman of the election supervision commitee, told reporters after meeting President Suharto.
He said 49 people had died under various circumstances during the campaign.
On Sunday, police fired tear gas and rubber bullets to disperse supporters of the PPP in two towns in Central Java as tensions rose ahead of the elections.

The PPP has repeatedly defied a ban on street parades during the campaign period. The party campaigned across the main island of Java on Sunday and brought tens of thousands of supporters onto the streets in major cities, including Jakarta.
Central Java province has been particularly tense following clashes between PPP and Golkar supporters.

Political analysts have said the alliance between Megawati supporters and the PPP is perhaps the only interesting feature of an otherwise lacklustre campaign, but stressed that it would have little effect on Golkar's expected easy win.

Golkar, in power for the last 30 years under President Suharto, is seeking to push its share of the vote to more than 70 percent from the 68 percent it won at the last polls in 1992. The PPP won 17 percent and the PDI 15 percent.
